notes: Route that works: the site's own 'Ultimas' listing, https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/ultimas?page=N (Drupal pager, 0-based, HTTP 200, 9-14 cards per page). Every card carries the outlet's publication stamp in its markup: plus dom, 25/10/2026 - 11:10 inside div.data-publicacao, so the TSV date is the site-stated publication date (America/Sao_Paulo), not a crawl date. Crawl stops after 3 consecutive pages whose oldest card is older than 2026-09-25; 95 pages, ~4 min at polite_fetch's per-host rate. Result: 1268 unique URLs, every day 2026-09-25..2026-10-25 covered (min 16 on 2026-10-25, 41 on 2026-09-30, 20 on 2026-10-10, 52 on 2026-10-20), no duplicates, all dates inside the window; a second full run reproduced exactly 1268. Sample verification: 6 articles re-fetched across the three check days all HTTP 200, 4400-7200 chars of text, and equal to the listed date (e.g. 2026-09-30T10:45:00-03:00 for a URL listed 2026-09-30). Routes tried and rejected: robots.txt (200) lists NO Sitemap line and only disallows /includes/ /misc/ /modules/ /profiles/ /scripts/ /themes/ /admin/ /search/ /user/*; /sitemap.xml (200) is a Drupal xmlsitemap index of 16 pages totaling ~157k URLs but its newest lastmod is 2020-02-11 - the sitemap has been frozen since 2020, useless for 2026; /sitemap_index.xml, /sitemap-index.xml, /news-sitemap.xml, /sitemap-news.xml, /sitemap_news.xml, /google-news-sitemap.xml, /sitemap.xml.gz, /sitemap/news.xml all 404; /rss.xml (200) is stale (items from 2020-06), /feed returns the generic Drupal page, rss.ebc.com.br returns the same page; /jsonapi 404 (Drupal 7, no JSON:API); /ultimas-noticias 404; sitemap.xml?page=1..16 all 200 with 9833-10000 urls each but lastmod max 2020. Fetching each article page for article:published_time instead of the listing would have needed ~1300 requests (25+ min), so the listing's own dates were used. A previous worker's partial script (homepage /?page=N plus per-article fetches) left 32 URLs; it was replaced. All HTTP goes through scrapers/polite_fetch.fetch; the script prints per-day counts and writes URLYYYY-MM-DD sorted by date then URL, no header.
